sa: स्वभावम् एके कवयो वदन्ति कालं तथान्ये परिमुह्यमानाः  ।
देवस्यैष महिमा तु लोके येनेदं भ्राम्यते ब्रह्मचक्रम् ॥
iast: svabhāvam eke kavayo vadanti kālaṃ tathānye parimuhyamānāḥ  ।
devasyaiṣa mahimā tu loke yenedaṃ bhrāmyate brahmacakram ॥

alt.text: ’Tis Nature and Self-existence, say one school of the Seers. Nay, ’tis Time, say another; both are deceived and bewildered. ’Tis the Majesty of the Lord in the world of His creatures whereby the Wheel of the Eternal whirleth about continually.

words: to be bewildered or perplexed; to go astray; to fail
to confuse; to move or roam about; to cause to wander

tr.text: Some deluded thinkers speak of Nature, and others of time, as the force that revolves this wheel of Brahman. But really all this is only the glory of God manifested in the world.

sa: येनावृतं नित्यम् इदं हि सर्वं ज्ञः कालकालो गुणी सर्वविद्यः  ।
तेनेशितं कर्म विवर्तते ह पृथिव्याप्तेजोऽनिलखानि चिन्त्यम् ॥
iast: yenāvṛtaṃ nityam idaṃ hi sarvaṃ jñaḥ kālakālo guṇī sarvavidyaḥ  ।
teneśitaṃ karma vivartate ha pṛthivyāptejo’nilakhāni cintyam ॥

alt.text: He envelopeth this whole Universe with Himself for ever, He that knoweth, Maker of Time, & the Modes of Nature dwell in Him; yea, all things He discerneth and by His governance the Law of Works revolveth in its cycle. Earth, water, fire, air, ether, of these thou shalt consider (as the substance wherein it turneth).

words: containing parts; cosisisting of parts; endowed with good qualities or merits

tr.text: It should be known that energy assumes various forms such as earth, water, light, air and ether at the command of Him who is the master of Gunas and the maker of time, who is omniscient, who is Pure consciousness itself, and by whom all this is ever enveloped.

sa: तत् कर्म कृत्वा विनिवर्त्य भूयस् तत्त्वस्य तत्त्वेन समेत्य योगम्  ।
एकेन द्वाभ्यां त्रिभिर् अष्टभिर् वा कालेन चैवात्मगुणैश् च सूक्ष्मैः ॥
iast: tat karma kṛtvā vinivartya bhūyas tattvasya tattvena sametya yogam  ।
ekena dvābhyāṃ tribhir aṣṭabhir vā kālena caivātmaguṇaiś ca sūkṣmaiḥ ॥

alt.text: The Lord doeth works and resteth again from His works, one or two or three or eight He yoketh Himself with the Principle of things in their essence & with Time He yoketh Himself and with Self in its subtle workings.

words: to draw back (a missile); to avert; to divert (the gaze)

tr.text: After setting the creation in motion and withdrawing Himself from it, He unites the principle of Spirit with the principle of Matter – with one, with two, with three and with eight – through the mere instrumentality of time and their own inherent properties.

sa: आरभ्य कर्माणि गुणान्वितानि भावांश् च सर्वान् विनियोजयेद् यः  ।
तेषाम् अभावे कृतकर्मनाशः कर्मक्षये याति स तत्त्वतो ऽन्यः ॥
iast: ārabhya karmāṇi guṇānvitāni bhāvāṃś ca sarvān viniyojayed yaḥ  ।
teṣām abhāve kṛtakarmanāśaḥ karmakṣaye yāti sa tattvato ’nyaḥ ॥

alt.text: So He beginneth works, that are subject to the modes of Nature, and setteth all existences to their workings: & when these things are not, thereby cometh annihilation of work that hath been done; and with the perishing of work, He departeth out of them; for in His final truth He is other than they.

words: to lay or take hold of; to keep fast; to cling to
to entrust anything (acc.) to; to offer or present; to anything (acc.) to (dat.)

tr.text: He gives the start to the creation associated with the three Gunas of Nature, and others all things. Again, in the absence of the Gunas, He destroys all created objects, and after destruction, remains aloof in His essence.

sa: आदिः स संयोगनिमित्तहेतुः परस् त्रिकालाद् अकलो ऽपि दृष्टः  ।
तं विश्वरूपं भवभूतम् ईड्यं देवं स्वचित्तस्थम् उपास्य पूर्वम् ॥
iast: ādiḥ sa saṃyoganimittahetuḥ paras trikālād akalo ’pi dṛṣṭaḥ  ।
taṃ viśvarūpaṃ bhavabhūtam īḍyaṃ devaṃ svacittastham upāsya pūrvam ॥

alt.text: Lo we have beheld Him & He is the Beginning and the Cause of all Causes whereby these elements meet together & form ariseth; the past, the present and the future are this side of Him and Time hath no part in Him. Let us worship the Ancient of Days in our own hearts who sitteth. Let us wait upon God who must be adored, for the world is His shape and the Universe is but His becoming.

tr.text: By previously meditating as seated in one’s own heart, on that Adorable Being who appears as the universe, and who is the true source of all creatures, He can be perceived even though He is the primeval cause of the union (of Spirit with Matter), as well as the partless entity transcending the three divisions of time.

sa: स वृक्षकालाकृतिभिः परो ऽन्यो यस्मात् प्रपञ्चः परिवर्तते ऽयं  ।
धर्मावहं पापनुदं भगेशं ज्ञात्वात्मस्थम् अमृतं विश्वधाम ॥
iast: sa vṛkṣakālākṛtibhiḥ paro ’nyo yasmāt prapañcaḥ parivartate ’yaṃ  ।
dharmāvahaṃ pāpanudaṃ bhageśaṃ jñātvātmastham amṛtaṃ viśvadhāma ॥

alt.text: Time & Form and the Tree of Things, none of these is He for He is more than they & it is from Him that this Cosmos beginneth. We will know this Master of grace & glory for He cometh to us carrying righteousness in His hand & He driveth Sin from its strong places. We will know Him for He is in our Self & immortal & the World’s foundation.

tr.text: Knowing Him who is the origin and dissolution of the universe – the source of all virtue, the destroyer of all sins, the master of all good qualities, the immortal, and the abode of the universe – as seated in one’s own self, He is perceived as different from, and transcending, the tree of Samsara as well as time and form.

sa: तम् ईश्वराणां परमं महेश्वरं तं देवतानां परमं च दैवतं  ।
पतिं पतीनां परमं परस्ताद् विदाम देवं भुवनेशम् ईड्यम् ॥
iast: tam īśvarāṇāṃ paramaṃ maheśvaraṃ taṃ devatānāṃ paramaṃ ca daivataṃ  ।
patiṃ patīnāṃ paramaṃ parastād vidāma devaṃ bhuvaneśam īḍyam ॥

alt.text: We will know this Mightiest one who is far above all the mighty — this summit of the gods & their godhead, King of Kings and Lord of Lords, who towereth high above all summits & greatnesses. Let us learn of God for He is this World’s Master & all shall adore Him.

words: a husband; God; the Supreme Being
a husband; God; the Supreme Being
a god; a deity (often coll. "the deities"); image of a god

tr.text: May we realize Him – the transcendent and adorable master of the universe – who is the supreme lord over all the lords, the supreme God above all the gods, and the supreme ruler over all the rulers.

sa: न तस्य कार्यं करणं च विद्यते न तत्समश् चाभ्यधिकश् च दृश्यते  ।
परास्य शक्तिर् विविधैव श्रूयते स्वाभाविकी ज्ञानबलक्रिया च ॥
iast: na tasya kāryaṃ karaṇaṃ ca vidyate na tatsamaś cābhyadhikaś ca dṛśyate  ।
parāsya śaktir vividhaiva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñānabalakriyā ca ॥

alt.text: God needeth not to do anything neither hath He any organ of doing; there is none greater than He nor do we see any that is His equal — for His power is far over all, only men hear of it under a thousand names & various fashions. Lo the strength of Him and the works of Him and His Knowledge, they are self-efficient & their own cause & nature.

words: work or business to be done
belonging to or arising from one's own nature

tr.text: His has nothing to achieve for Himself, nor has He any organ of action. No one is seen equal or superior to Him. His great power alone is described in the Vedas to be of various kinds, and His knowledge, strength and action are described as inherent in Him.

sa: न तस्य कश्चित् पतिर् अस्ति लोके न चेशिता नैव च तस्य लिङ्गं  ।
स कारणं करणाधिपाधिपो न चास्य कश्चिज् जनिता न चाधिपः ॥
iast: na tasya kaścit patir asti loke na ceśitā naiva ca tasya liṅgaṃ  ।
sa kāraṇaṃ karaṇādhipādhipo na cāsya kaścij janitā na cādhipaḥ ॥

alt.text: He hath no master in all this world, there is none that shall rule over Him. Nor feature nor distinction hath He; for He is begetting cause and sovran over the lords of these natural organs, but Himself hath no begetter neither any sovran.

tr.text: No one in the world is His master, nor has anybody any control over Him. There is no sign by which He can be inferred. He is the cause of all, and the ruler of individual souls. He has no parent, nor is there any one who is His lord.

sa: यस् तन्तुनाभ इव तन्तुभिः प्रधानजैः स्वभावतः  ।
देव एकः स्वम् आवृणोति स नो दधाद् ब्रह्माप्ययम् ॥
iast: yas tantunābha iva tantubhiḥ pradhānajaiḥ svabhāvataḥ  ।
deva ekaḥ svam āvṛṇoti sa no dadhād brahmāpyayam ॥

alt.text: Even as is the spider that out of himself fashioneth his own web, so is God One & nought else existeth but by his own nature covereth Himself up in the threads He hath spun out of primal matter. May the One God ordain unto us departure into His Eternal.

words: a spider; a particular position of the hands; name of a son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra
a chief thing or person; the principal or first; primary matter or nature

tr.text: May the Supreme Being, who spontaneously covers Himself with the products of Nature, just as a spider does with the threads drawn from its own navel, grant us absorption in Brahman !

sa: एको देवः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः सर्वव्यापी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा  ।
कर्माध्यक्षः सर्वभूताधिवासः साक्षी चेता केवलो निर्गुणश् च ॥
iast: eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ sarvavyāpī sarvabhūtāntarātmā  ।
karmādhyakṣaḥ sarvabhūtādhivāsaḥ sākṣī cetā kevalo nirguṇaś ca ॥

alt.text: One God who alone is & He lurketh hidden in every creature for He pervadeth and is the inmost Self of all beings, He presideth over all work and is the home of all things living. He is the Mighty Witness who relateth thought with thought and again He is the Absolute in whom mood is not nor any attribute.

tr.text: God, who is one only, is hidden in all beings. He is all-pervading, and is the inner self of all creatures. He presides over all actions, and all beings reside in Him. He is the witness, and He is the Pure Consciousness free from the three Gunas of Nature.

takeaway: One God is hidden in every being, the witness of every act, the inner Self of all.

sa: एको वशी निष्क्रियाणां बहूणाम् एकं बीजं बहुधा यः करोति  ।
तम् आत्मस्थं ये ऽनुपश्यन्ति धीरास् तेषां सुखं शाश्वतं नेतरेषां ॥
iast: eko vaśī niṣkriyāṇāṃ bahūṇām ekaṃ bījaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti  ।
tam ātmasthaṃ ye ’nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣāṃ ॥

alt.text: One God & alone He controlleth the many who have themselves no separate work nor purpose; and He developeth one seed into many kinds of creatures; the strong-hearted behold God in their own Self, therefore for them is everlasting bliss and not for others.

words: in many ways or parts or forms or directions

tr.text: Those wise men, who ever feel in their own hearts the presence of Him who is the one ruler of the inactive many, and who makes the one seed manifold – to them belongs eternal happiness, and to none else.

sa: नित्यो नित्यानां चेतनश् चेतनानाम् एको बहूनां यो विदधाति कामान्  ।
तत् कारणं सांख्ययोगाधिगम्यं ज्ञात्वा देवं मुच्यते सर्वपाशैः ॥
iast: nityo nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān  ।
tat kāraṇaṃ sāṃkhyayogādhigamyaṃ jñātvā devaṃ mucyate sarvapāśaiḥ ॥

alt.text: One Eternal of all these that pass & are not, One conscious in all consciousnesses; He being One ordereth the desires of many; He alone is the great Source to which Sankhya and Yoga bring us. If thou know God thou shalt break free from every sort of bondage.

words: name of one of the three great divisions of Hindū philosophy

tr.text: He is the eternal among the eternal and the intelligent among all that are intelligent. Though one, He grants the desires of the many. One is released from all fetters on realizing Him, the cause of all, who is comprehensible through philosophy and religious discipline.

sa: न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतो ऽयम् अग्निः  ।
तम् एव भान्तम् अनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वम् इदं विभाति ॥
iast: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto ’yam agniḥ  ।
tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti ॥

alt.text: There the sun cannot shine and the moon has no splendour; the stars are blind; there our lightnings flash not neither any earthly fire; all that is bright is but the shadow of His brightness and by His shining all this shineth.

tr.text: The sun does not shine there; neither the moon, nor the stars. There these lightnings shine not – how then this fire ? Because He shines, everything shines after Him. By His light all this shines.

sa: एको हंसो भुवनस्यास्य मध्ये स एवाग्निः सलिले संनिविष्टः  ।
तम् एव विदित्वाति मृत्युम् एति नान्यः पन्था विद्यते ऽयनाय ॥
iast: eko haṃso bhuvanasyāsya madhye sa evāgniḥ salile saṃniviṣṭaḥ  ।
tam eva viditvāti mṛtyum eti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate ’yanāya ॥

alt.text: One Swan of Being in the heart of all this Universe & He is Fire that lieth deep in the heart of water. By Knowledge of Him, the soul passeth beyond the pursuit of Death and there is no other road for the great passage.

tr.text: The one destroyer of ignorance in the midst of this universe, He alone is the fire which is stationed in water. Realizing Him alone one overcomes death. There is no other path for emancipation.

sa: स विश्वकृद् विश्वविद् आत्मयोनिर् ज्ञः कालकालो गुणी सर्वविद्यः  ।
प्रधानक्षेत्रज्ञपतिर् गुणेशः संसारमोक्षस्थितिबन्धहेतुः ॥
iast: sa viśvakṛd viśvavid ātmayonir jñaḥ kālakālo guṇī sarvavidyaḥ  ।
pradhānakṣetrajñapatir guṇeśaḥ saṃsāramokṣasthitibandhahetuḥ ॥

alt.text: He hath made all and knoweth all; for He is the womb out of which Self ariseth, & being possessed of the Nature Moods He becometh Time’s Maker and discerneth all things. And Matter is subject to Him & the Spirit in Man that cogniseth His field of matter & the modes of Nature are His servants. He therefore is the cause of this coming into phenomena & of the release from phenomena — & because of Him is their endurance & because of Him is their bondage.

words: containing parts; cosisisting of parts; endowed with good qualities or merits
a chief thing or person; the principal or first; primary matter or nature
standing upright or firmly; not falling; standing

tr.text: He is the creator of everything as well as the knower of everything. He is His own source, He is all-knowing, and He is the destroyer of time. He is the repository of all good qualities, and the master of all sciences. He is the controller of Matter and Spirit, and the lord of the Gunas. He is the cause of liberation from the cycle of birth and death, and of bondage which results in its continuance.

sa: स तन्मयो ह्य् अमृत ईशसंस्थो ज्ञः सर्वगो भुवनस्यास्य गोप्ता  ।
स ईशे अस्य जगतो नित्यम् एव नान्यो हेतुर् विद्यत ईशनाय ॥
iast: sa tanmayo hy amṛta īśasaṃstho jñaḥ sarvago bhuvanasyāsya goptā  ।
sa īśe asya jagato nityam eva nānyo hetur vidyata īśanāya ॥

alt.text: Lo He is Immortal because He is utter existence; but He houseth Himself in the Lord & is the Knower, the Omnipresent that standeth on guard over this His universe, yea He ruleth all this moving world for ever and for ever, and there is no other source of lordship and kingliness.

words: staying or abiding with; shape; form

tr.text: He is the soul of the universe, He is immortal, and His is the rulership. He is the all knowing, the all-pervading, the protector of the universe, the eternal ruler. None else is there efficient to govern the world eternally.

sa: यो ब्रह्माणं विदधाति पूर्वं यो वै वेदांश् च प्रहिणोति तस्मै  ।
तं ह देवम् आत्मबुद्धिप्रकाशं मुमुक्षुर् वै शरणम् अहं प्रपद्ये ॥
iast: yo brahmāṇaṃ vidadhāti pūrvaṃ yo vai vedāṃś ca prahiṇoti tasmai  ।
taṃ ha devam ātmabuddhiprakāśaṃ mumukṣur vai śaraṇam ahaṃ prapadye ॥

alt.text: He ordained Brahma the Creator from of old and sent forth unto him the Veda, I will hasten unto God who standeth self-revealed in the Spirit & in the Understanding. I will take refuge in the Lord for my salvation;

words: to urge on; to incite; to direct
desirous of freeing; wishing to deliver from (abl.)
shelter; place of shelter or refuge or rest; hut

tr.text: He who at the beginning of creation projected Brahma (Universal Consciousness), who delivered the Vedas unto him, who constitutes the supreme bridge of immortality, who is the partless, free from actions, tranquil, faultless, taintless and resembles the fire that has consumed its fuel – seeking liberation I go for refuge to that Effulgent One, whose light turns the understanding towards the Atman.

sa: निष्कलं निष्क्रियं शान्तं निरवद्यं निरञ्जनम्  ।
अमृतस्य परं सेतुं दग्धेन्धनम् इवानलम् ॥
iast: niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ śāntaṃ niravadyaṃ nirañjanam  ।
amṛtasya paraṃ setuṃ dagdhendhanam ivānalam ॥

alt.text: Who hath neither parts nor works for He is utterly tranquil, faultless, stainless, therefore He is the one great bridge that carrieth us over to Immortality, even as when a fire hath burnt all its fuel.

words: fire; the god of fire; digestive power

tr.text: He who at the beginning of creation projected Brahma (Universal Consciousness), who delivered the Vedas unto him, who constitutes the supreme bridge of immortality, who is the partless, free from actions, tranquil, faultless, taintless and resembles the fire that has consumed its fuel – seeking liberation I go for refuge to that Effulgent One, whose light turns the understanding towards the Atman.

sa: यदा चर्मवद् आकाशं वेष्टयिष्यन्ति मानवाः  ।
तदा देवम् अविज्ञाय दुःखस्यान्तो भविष्यति ॥
iast: yadā carmavad ākāśaṃ veṣṭayiṣyanti mānavāḥ  ।
tadā devam avijñāya duḥkhasyānto bhaviṣyati ॥

alt.text: When the sons of men shall fold up ether like a skin and wrap the heavens round them like a garment, then alone without knowledge of the Lord our God shall the misery of the World have an ending.

words: to wrap up; to envelop; to enclose

tr.text: Only when men shall roll up the sky like a skin, will there be an end of misery for them without realizing God.

sa: तपःप्रभावाद् देवप्रसादात् ब्रह्म ह श्वेताश्वतरो ऽथ विद्वान्  ।
अत्याश्रमिभ्यः परमं पवित्रं प्रोवाच सम्यग् ऋषिसङ्घजुष्टम् ॥
iast: tapaḥprabhāvād devaprasādāt brahma ha śvetāśvataro ’tha vidvān  ।
atyāśramibhyaḥ paramaṃ pavitraṃ provāca samyag ṛṣisaṅghajuṣṭam ॥

alt.text: By the might of his devotion & the grace of God in his being Svetasvatara hereafter knew the Eternal & he came to the renouncers of the worldly life and truly declared unto them the Most High & Pure God, to whom the companies of seers resort for ever.

words: name of a teacher; pl.his school
an ascetic of the highest degree
any collection or assemblage; heap; multitude

tr.text: Himself realizing Brahman by the power of self-control and concentration of mind, as well as by the grace of God, the sage Svetasvatara expounded well to the highest order of Sannyasins, the truth of that supremely holy Brahman resorted to by all the seers.

sa: वेदान्ते परमं गुह्यं पुराकल्पे प्रचोदितम्  ।
नाप्रशान्ताय दातव्यं नापुत्रायाशिष्याय वा पुनः ॥
iast: vedānte paramaṃ guhyaṃ purākalpe pracoditam  ।
nāpraśāntāya dātavyaṃ nāputrāyāśiṣyāya vā punaḥ ॥

alt.text: This is the great secret of the Vedanta which was declared in former times, not on hearts untranquilled to be squandered nor men sonless nor on one who hath no disciples.

words: a former creation; former age; the performance of sacrificial acts in former times
to make haste; to excite; to inspire

tr.text: This highest mysticism, expounded in the Vedanta in a former age, should not be taught to one whose passions have not been subdued, nor to one who is not a worthy son, nor to an unworthy disciple.

sa: यस्य देवे परा भक्तिर् यथा देवे तथा गुरौ  ।
तस्यैते कथिता ह्य् अर्थाः प्रकाशन्ते महात्मनः प्रकाशन्ते महात्मनः ॥
iast: yasya deve parā bhaktir yathā deve tathā gurau  ।
tasyaite kathitā hy arthāḥ prakāśante mahātmanaḥ prakāśante mahātmanaḥ ॥

alt.text: But whosoever hath supreme love & adoration for the Lord and as for the Lord, so likewise for the Master, to that Mighty Soul these great matters when they are told become clear of themselves, yea to the Great Soul of him they are manifest.

tr.text: These truths, when taught, shine forth only in that high-souled one who has supreme devotion to God, and an equal degree of devotion to the spiritual teacher. They shine forth in that high-souled one only.
